subject: Follow-up: marketplace procurement & payment route — AWS preference confirmed?
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sana Iqbal <sana@novafin.io>, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: marketplace procurement & payment route — AWS preference confirmed?

Thanks again for the conversation earlier, Sana and Tom — good to meet you both. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can line up procurement and commercial next steps.

Call summary (short):
- Use case: Acme Health wants a patient-facing summarization and triage assistant for intake; expected 50k monthly active sessions initially, ~3–6 tokens per session on avg.
- Primary requirement: data residency + audit logging for PHI-adjacent telemetry (you mentioned security controls matter).
- Procurement preference: you said procurement prefers standard PO flow and team is evaluating use of AWS Marketplace for faster procurement.

Open items / asks:
1) Can you confirm whether procurement will accept an AWS Marketplace purchase order (i.e., transactable via marketplace) or if they require a direct PO to Redwood?
2) Who is the procurement POC (name + email) we should loop in for SOW/PO/contract cadence?
3) Expected signature/timeline target from procurement (weeks) so we can map pricing cadence and reserved capacity if needed.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- I’ll drop a mutual action plan that maps milestones (security review → procurement → PO/signature → pilot).
- Lauren (cc’d) will pull marketplace pricing and onboarding checklist for AWS and GCP (if you want both options).
- Dev will prepare a short SOW/contract stub and an options summary for PO vs credit-card (pros/cons, lead times).

Attachments: Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (draft), Redwood_SAAS_CONTRACT_v1.pdf (starter) — see attached stubs.

If you can reply inline on items 1–3 above by EOD Wed 10/14 that would let us keep to the pilot timeline you mentioned (late Nov).

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

---
On Mon, 12 Oct 2026 at 12:10 PM Sana Iqbal <sana@novafin.io> wrote:
> Hi Rafael — thanks, appreciated.
> 
> A few quick clarifications inline:
> 1) Procurement prefers PO but has used AWS Marketplace before — marketplace would be ideal because it shortens our internal approval steps.
> 2) Procurement POC: Tom Reilly (tom.reilly@acmehealth.com) — I’ve cc’d him to validate.
> 3) Timeline: procurement is aiming for signature in 3–4 weeks, dependent on legal review.
> 
> We do need to confirm whether Redwood can accept a marketplace order that covers reserved capacity or if that requires a direct contract.
> 
> Cheers,
> Sana
>

From: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@acmehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Sana Iqbal <sana@novafin.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: marketplace procurement & payment route — AWS preference confirmed?

Rafael / Sana — confirming procurement stance:
- We prefer AWS Marketplace where possible; it reduces approval friction for purchasing teams.
- For committed / reserved capacity (longer-term commitments) procurement may still request a direct PO to vendor depending on discount level.
- I can take point on procurement and will share Acme’s standard PO template and any specific security evidence requests.

Next for me: I’ll send the PO template and list of required contract clauses (SLA, data handling, breach notification) by end of day Tue 10/13. If Redwood can provide a marketplace-compatible SKU/listing and a standard MSA + SOW we can likely transact through AWS.

Tom Reilly
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Health
tom.reilly@acmehealth.com
+1 (617) 555-1987

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@acmehealth.com>, Sana Iqbal <sana@novafin.io>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: marketplace procurement & payment route — AWS preference confirmed?

Thanks Tom — adding a quick internal note on the Redwood side.

Action items I’ll own:
- Confirm whether our current AWS Marketplace onboarding supports reserved SKU mapping (short answer: yes but needs partner onboarding work). I’ll attach the onboarding checklist.
- Prepare two pricing paths: (A) Marketplace listing (no bespoke contract, faster, payment via AWS billing) (B) Direct PO flow (custom MSA + SOW, supports reserved capacity & discounting).
- Estimate lead times: Marketplace listing + procurement closure ~2–3 weeks once marketplace paperwork is complete; Direct PO with legal review + discount negotiation typically 3–6 weeks.

Dev — can you prepare a one-page SOW stub and a summarized comparison (PO vs card/marketplace) for Rafael to send to Acme? I’ll also assemble the onboarding checklist and marketplace SKU notes.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Partnerships & GTM Ops | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@acmehealth.com>, Sana Iqbal <sana@novafin.io>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: marketplace procurement & payment route — AWS preference confirmed?

Attached: AWS_Marketplace_Onboarding_Checklist.docx and a draft SOW (one-page).

Quick SOW summary (for the pilot):
- Scope: 8-week pilot, inference service for intake assistant, up to 50k active sessions/month, data logged with audit-only telemetry (no long-term PHI retention).
- Deliverables: sandbox endpoint, performance SLAs for 95th% latency, onboarding runbook, monitoring setup in Redwood Console.
- Commercial options:
  * Marketplace (pay via AWS): standard SKU pricing $0.0025 / token equivalent (example), onboarding fee waived for first 3 months. Pros: fastest procurement; Cons: limited custom discounts.
  * Direct PO (invoice): monthly invoice; supports reserved capacity commitments and volume discounts; requires MSA + SOW signature.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Tom to share PO template and legal clause list (you indicated EOD Tue).
2) Acme to confirm marketplace vs direct PO preference; if marketplace, we kick off AWS onboarding and map a SKU.
3) Redwood to supply final MSA + SOW or marketplace listing details depending on route.

If that lines up, Rafael — can you confirm you’ll send the mutual action plan + SOW stub to the Acme procurement thread and ask for PO template from Tom? I’ll update the attachments here.

Best,
Dev Patel
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments (stubs): AWS_Marketplace_Onboarding_Checklist.docx, Redwood_SOW_draft_onepage.pdf
